accepted.question_text: For the hard-core lattice gas (independent-set model) on a countably infinite graph G=(V,E) of maximum degree Delta, with vertex fugacities {w_x} and Gibbs measures defined for nonnegative fugacities, is it true that uniqueness of the infinite-volume Gibbs measure holds whenever 0 <= w_x <= (1-epsilon)*(Delta-1)^(Delta-1)/(Delta-2)^Delta for all vertices x and some epsilon>0 (possibly even epsilon=0)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.1 For any countably infinite graph G of maximum degree Delta, the hard-core lattice gas on G has a unique Gibbs measure whenever 0 <= w_x <= (1-epsilon) x (Delta-1)^(Delta-1)/(Delta-2)^Delta ... for all vertices x, for some epsilon > 0. [Perhaps this is true even with epsilon = 0.]

accepted.question_text: Consider the same hard-core lattice-gas setting as in Conjecture 2.1, but restricted to non-regular trees with all fugacities equal. Can one prove the Conjecture 2.1 uniqueness claim in that tree setting?

evidence.quote: It seems to be an open problem to prove Conjecture 2.1 even when G is a non-regular tree and the w_x are all equal.

accepted.question_text: In the hard-core/repulsive-gas context, Dobrushin's approach proves nonvanishing of the partition function Z first and then analyticity/convergence of log Z. Can this approach be extended so that it works without assuming hard-core self-repulsion?

evidence.quote: It is an interesting open question to know whether this approach can be made to work without the assumption of hard-core self-repulsion.

accepted.question_text: For the hard-core lattice-gas partition function Z(w) on graphs of maximum degree Delta, what is the largest complex domain containing w=0 such that Z(w) is zero-free for all such graphs? This should account for both the equal-fugacity case and the unequal-fugacity case (where one asks for domains D such that Z(w) != 0 whenever every vertex fugacity w_x belongs to D).

evidence.quote: Question 2.4 What is the largest complex domain containing w = 0 on which Z(w) is zero-free for all graphs of maximum degree Delta? [This question has two versions, depending on whether the w_x are assumed equal or unequal.]

accepted.question_text: If G is claw-free (has no induced K_{1,3}), must every zero of the hard-core lattice-gas partition function Z(w) be a negative real number?
accepted.context_brief: Claw-free graphs and real negative zeros

evidence.quote: Conjecture 2.5 (Hamidoune [28], Stanley [66]) If G is claw-free (i.e. has no induced subgraph K1,3), then all the zeros of Z(w) are negative real.

accepted.question_text: For the hard-core lattice gas on general graphs, what happens at non-small fugacity w: when does one have uniqueness versus nonuniqueness of infinite-volume Gibbs measures as a function of w, what are the large-w Gibbs measures, and are the phase transitions first-order or second-order?

evidence.quote: Finally, one may ask: What happens when the fugacity w is not small? In particular, one would like to understand the uniqueness or nonuniqueness of the infinite-volume Gibbs measure as a function of w, the nature of the large-w Gibbs measures, and whether the phase transition(s) is/are first-order or second-order.

accepted.question_text: For the q-coloring model (zero-temperature antiferromagnetic Potts model), prove uniqueness of the infinite-volume Gibbs measure and exponential decay of correlations in specific unresolved cases, including q=3 on the hexagonal lattice and q=4,5,6 on the square lattice.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.2 Prove uniqueness of the infinite-volume Gibbs measure and exponential decay of correlations for q = 3 on the hexagonal lattice, q = 4, 5, 6 on the square lattice, etc.

accepted.question_text: In the q-coloring model on bounded-degree graphs, what is the sharp threshold in q versus Delta separating guaranteed uniqueness from possible nonuniqueness of infinite-volume Gibbs measures? In particular, is the classical q>2Delta condition sharp, or can the true borderline be as low as q>Delta (as suggested by tree behavior)?

evidence.quote: It is natural to ask whether the borderline 2Delta is sharp ... Even for the Delta-regular tree, the correct borderline is not known ... For trees the Gibbs measure may well be unique as soon as q > Delta; and it is at least conceivable that this is the sharp borderline for general graphs.

accepted.question_text: For chromatic-polynomial zeros of graphs with maximum degree Delta, what is the optimal sharp bound C_opt(Delta) on their modulus, and what can be proved about zero-free or root-location regions in the complex q-plane beyond discs centered at q=0?

evidence.quote: Question 3.4 (a) What is the sharp bound Copt(Delta)? Might 2Delta work? Is Copt(3) = 3? What about regions of the q-plane other than discs centered at q = 0?

accepted.question_text: For Glauber dynamics of the hard-core lattice gas, what is the precise relation between rapid-mixing proofs obtained by probabilistic coupling and proofs obtained via Dobrushin-type analytic methods, specifically in terms of identifying the norm/seminorm in which the transition operator P is contractive (norm < 1) on functions modulo constants?
accepted.context_brief: Coupling vs Dobrushin for mixing proofs

evidence.quote: I'd like to raise a general question: What is the relation between proofs of rapid mixing by coupling methods and by the Dobrushin uniqueness method? ... we conclude that the transition matrix P ... has norm <= beta+epsilon < 1 in some norm or other - but which norm?

accepted.question_text: For Glauber dynamics at complex fugacity on finite graphs of maximum degree Delta, does there exist a complex domain D_Delta containing [0, 1/(Delta-1)) such that the spectral radius of the transition matrix P (on the quotient space modulo constants) satisfies spr(P)<1 for every such graph whenever w lies in D_Delta?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.2 There exists a complex domain DDelta containing the interval [0, 1/(Delta - 1) ) such that spr(P) < 1 holds for all graphs G of maximum degree Delta whenever w belongs to DDelta.

accepted.question_text: Can one construct a unified seminorm framework that interpolates between the total-oscillation seminorm and the exponentially weighted Fourier-coefficient seminorm used in Theorem 4.3, in order to prove spr(P)<1 on a domain containing both the disc given by inequality (4.5) and the real interval [0,1/(Delta-1))?

evidence.quote: The question is: How to interpolate smoothly between these two radically different seminorms ... in order to prove spr(P) < 1 for a domain DDelta containing both the disc (4.5) and the interval [0, 1/(Delta - 1) )?

accepted.question_text: For the Wang-Swendsen-Kotecky (WSK) dynamics for zero-temperature Potts colorings on periodic lattices, for which lattice sizes n is the dynamics ergodic in the currently unresolved cases q=4 on an n x n periodic triangular lattice and q=3 on an n x n Kagome lattice?

evidence.quote: All other cases are open (to the best of my knowledge). In particular, we would like to know for which values of n (if any) the WSK dynamics is ergodic for q = 4 on an n x n periodic triangular lattice, or for q = 3 on an n x n Kagome lattice.

accepted.question_text: For the full WSK algorithm in the q=3 Potts antiferromagnet on n x n periodic square lattices at and down to zero temperature, can one rigorously prove rapid mixing behavior consistent with the numerically observed constant-time mixing (absence of critical slowing down)?
accepted.context_brief: Rigorous proof of fast WSK mixing

evidence.quote: For the full WSK algorithm, numerical data strongly suggest that there is constant-time mixing ... for the q = 3 model on n x n periodic square lattices ... It would be wonderful to be able to prove something!
